newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek TN, SN rates fall on inflows, focus on auction.
newsitem.headline: Greek TN, SN rates fall on inflows, focus on auction.

text.p: Greek tomnext and spotnext rates were trading 30 to 40 basis points lower in late dealings with the rest of the yield curve fluctuating narrowly and the focus was on Friday's auction of FRNs and bonds, dealers said.
"Tomnext and spotnext are down 30 to 40 basis points in late trade on ecu inflows," said a dealer at a state bank.
Other traders predicted the market would turn long on Friday and Monday on a combination of forex inflows and seasonal deposits from Greece's post office.
"The market will turn long tomorrow and Monday on a 200 billion drachma liquidity boost from forex inflows and the usual ELTA (post office) deposits," said a trader at a private bank.
The central bank pumped overnight liquidity into the market at an unchanged 13.40 percent.
Dealers said the market focus was shifting to Friday's auction of FRNs and three-year coupon bonds.

An informal Reuters poll among banks, mutuals funds and brokerages predicted an average bid of 100.20 for the floaters and 98.7 for the three-year bond. The poll produced a mode of 100.30 for the FRNs and 99.30 for the three-year bonds.
Greece will auction about 200 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs with the first coupon at 13.40 percent, the 12-month T-bill rate set at 12 percent and the spread at 10 basis points on Friday.

It will also auction 100 billion drachmas of three-year, 11 percent coupon bonds on November 12. Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told Reuters on Wednesday that he expected investors to welcome the paper.
The mark was quoted at 157.75/85 drachmas from Thursday's 157.825 fix, the dollar at 236.72/82 drachmas from 236.460 and the Ecu at 303.22/32 from 303.390 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is easier. Banks sold 30 to 40 million ecus for drachmas at today's fixing," said a forex dealer.
